\section[increíble]{increíble — incredible, unbelievable}

\label{lesson:ES-C508-increible}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for the inhabitant, then the Spanish for the debate.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: increíble}
\textbf{increíble} — \textquotedblleft{}incredible, unbelievable\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
¡Es increíble!
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{It is incredible!}
\end{quote}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for reading notices, forms and messages.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[conocido]{conocido — well known; an acquaintance}

\label{lesson:ES-C508-conocido}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for incredible, then the Spanish for independent.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: conocido}
\textbf{conocido} — \textquotedblleft{}well known; an acquaintance\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Es un cantante muy conocido.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{He is a very well-known singer.}
\end{quote}

As a noun, \emph{un conocido} is someone you know, not quite a friend.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for reading notices, forms and messages.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[actual]{actual — current, present-day}

\label{lesson:ES-C508-actual}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for independent, then the Spanish for well known.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: actual}
\textbf{actual} — \textquotedblleft{}current, present-day\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
El precio actual es de diez euros.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The current price is ten euros.}
\end{quote}

A false friend: actual in English is \emph{real}.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for reading notices, forms and messages.
\end{grammarlens}
